items.abstract_or_text: Highlights - Known Issues - Multi-GPU (TP2) streaming or RPC executor workloads may hang during worker initialization when MPI worker pools are reused across LLM instances (observed on H100). - DeepSeek MLA models on SM120/SM121 GPUs (for example RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell) may crash with an illegal memory access when CUDA graphs are captured with BF16 BMM. - GPT-OSS models on SM120 GPUs may fail with attention data parallelism when automatic communication selects NCCL EP for unsupported hidden sizes. - Qwen3 models with tied embeddings (for example Qwen3-0.6B) may fail at model construction when attention data parallelism is enabled with TP greater than 1. - OpenTelemetry tracing may export additional FastAPI spans when FastAPI 0.142 or newer is installed. - Model Support - Add GLM-5.3-Flash (glm5_next) support #19136 - Support K-EXAONE-2 in the PyTorch backend #17067 - Add Qwen-Image-Layered with FP8 and Cache-DiT support #16889 - Load static FP8 Cosmos3 Nano/Super checkpoints without re-quantization #17476 - Enable EVS for Nemotron Super 3.5 VL and EVS handoff for Nemotron-H in EPD #19648, #19702 - Load quantized Nemotron-H MTP heads #19558, #19597 - Add MiniMax-M3 NVFP4 KV cache support with query-length buffer reuse and a native draft KV view #19422, #19768, #19731 - Add MiniMax H3 ref2va mode and Turbo LoRA tensor-name mapping #19657, #19701 - Route Qwen3.6/3.8 vision-language checkpoints to the generic Qwen3.5 VLM wrapper #19892 - API - Remove the Python backend of KVCacheManagerV2 (BREAKING) #19154 - Migrate LlmRequest fields to Python (BREAKING) #19484 - Add command-line configuration overrides #19555 - Report per-request speculative-decoding acceptance in responses #19311 - Return OpenAI-style errors when a request exceeds the context length #19457 - Add a per-model serving-extension registry to the OpenAI server #19499 - Ship the OpenEngine gRPC bindings in the wheel, so no separate package install is needed #19371 - Feature - Add a Mooncake store pool, CLI, and V2 scheduler preemption (part 1) #19235 - Add sparse KV cache configuration, tier-aware locking, and offload with GPU metadata publication; prepare DeepSeek V4 attention for sparse KV offload #19580, #19821, #19502 - Add VisualGen VSA and SOL sparse attention on PrimTS block-sparse FMHA and integrate updated SM90 SageAttention kernels #18079, #18496 - Support beam search with the C++ KVCacheManagerV2 #17306 - Stream C++ KV events with multimodal payloads #19359 - Add model startup stage timing metrics, sampled iteration statistics, and items.abstract_or_text: ## Decision models in the CLI Decision models can now be used directly from the terminal with `ollama run` — ask yes/no questions, classify text into labels, or score against a rubric: `ollama run nimble --ask "Is a refund being requested?" < ticket.txt` ## What's Changed * Kev decision models are now supported by the MLX runner on Apple silicon * `ollama launch` can now be used with usage credits without upgrading to a paid plan * `ollama launch codex` now includes locally installed Ollama models in its model picker. Use `/model` within the Codex CLI to swap models. * Improved inference performance by reusing verified manifests and already loaded models * Added support for multimodal embeddings through llama-server * Fixed loading multimodal embedding models with small context windows * Improved Gemma 4 prefill performance on NVIDIA GPUs with the MLX runner * MLX runner now clips long Laya states instead of rejecting them * Improved speculative decoding reliability in the MLX runner, including recurrent state handling after rollback * Updated llama.cpp with native decision model support * Updated README and documentation with clearer privacy and cloud-services wording **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ollama/ollama/compare/v0.40.3...v0.40.4

items.title: b11630
items.abstract_or_text: ggml: fix conv_1d result layout for batched input (#28738) * ggml: fix conv_1d result layout for batched input The GEMM behind conv_1d folds the batch into its rows, so the product sits in memory as [OL, N, OC] while the reshape claims [OL, OC, N]. The shape is right and the contents are transposed, so nothing fires: no assert, no abort, the graph just runs and the channels come out interleaved with the batches. With N == 1 the two readings describe the same buffer, which is why the three vocoders in the tree never hit it, they all squeeze to 2d right after the call. Reshape to the real layout and permute OC and N back. The N == 1 path keeps its direct reshape, so the current callers build the same graph and pay for no extra copy. tests/test-conv-1d.cpp compares one batched convolution against N single batch convolutions built from the same weight and the same input slices. Five of the seven geometries fail before this change and all seven pass after. N == 1 and OC == 1 pass either way, since swapping two dimensions when one of them is 1 changes nothing. The batched path matters to downstream audio projects where several synthesis lanes share a single graph. Nothing in mtmd batches a vocoder today, each one streams one flow and carries its left context between calls, but the op is correct now if one of them grows a lane dimension. * ggml: build the same conv_1d graph for every batch size Address review from ggerganov: drop the N == 1 branch of ggml_conv_1d. The GEMM result is always reshaped to [OC, N, OL] and permuted back, as ggml_conv_2d does, so every batch size builds the same graph. For N == 1 this adds a cont on an already ordered tensor. **Website:** - **Attestations:** - **macOS/iOS:** - [macOS Apple Silicon (arm64)](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/download/b11630/llama-b11630-bin-macos-arm64.tar.gz) - items.abstract_or_text: graph: skip the LM head for pooled embeddings (#30445) * graph: skip the LM head for pooled embeddings A context that extracts pooled embeddings outputs one vector per sequence, but every model still expanded its LM head, so the graph computed n_vocab logits per token and the context kept a host buffer for them. The models now only declare t_logits, and set_outputs() expands it unless the context extracts embeddings with a pooling type other than NONE. Since the toggle changes the graph shape for a pooled context, set_embeddings() schedules a re-reserve in that case. * graph: drop the redundant t_embd expand Address review from @CISC: with embeddings on, build_pooling() already expands its output for every pooling type, and a decoder graph without embeddings does not read t_embd, so set_outputs() only expands t_logits. * graph: add build_logits() for the LM head output Address review from @ggerganov: the LM head is expanded by a dedicated build_logits(), called from llama_model::build_graph() like build_pooling(), and set_outputs() only marks the outputs again. * graph: call build_logits() before build_sampling() Address review from @ggerganov: build_sampling() reads t_logits, so the LM head is built first. A pooled context then skips the sampling layers too, since it has no logits to sample from. * nit **Website:** - **Attestations:** - **macOS/iOS:** - [macOS Apple Silicon (arm64)](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/download/b11597/llama-b11597-bin-macos-arm64.tar.gz) - items.abstract_or_text: tests : consolidate context state tests into test-llama-context (#30023) * tests : consolidate the context state tests into test-llama-context test-save-load-state, test-recurrent-state-rollback and test-state-restore-fragmented check the same object from three places: the KV cache and the recurrent state of a llama_context, saved, loaded, copied, rolled back. Each had its own main, its own loop over the models, its own copy of the token and the comparison helpers, and a run of all three loaded the same models several times. They are one binary now, and the case is the unit of the test: tests/llama-context/test-case.h the interface a case implements tests/llama-context/cases-kv.cpp the cases of the KV cache tests/llama-context/cases-rs.cpp the cases of the recurrent state tests/llama-context/test-util.cpp tokens, generation, comparison tests/llama-context/test-runner.cpp the models of a case, on threads tests/llama-context/test-log.cpp the log file of a model A run is a table: a row per model, a column per case, a cell holds the verdict of that pair. The models load on several threads (-j, --threads, min(cores, 4) by default), the table is printed when it is complete and the log of a model that failed is printed after it, in the order of the rows. A case returns a verdict and the reason for it, and the runner is the only one who reports - the test does not use tests/testing.h, a run over 130 models is a matrix of verdicts and not a tree of subtests. Staging no longer travels through the environment: llama_model_set_attn_rot replaces the LLAMA_ATTN_ROT_DISABLE variable, which a model loaded in one thread used to change for the models the other threads were loading, and llama_memory_get_buffers is added for the cases that copy the buffers of a memory. common_log_set_stdo keeps the console quiet while the table is being built. ggml_aligned_malloc allocates with posix_memalign when the thread sanitizer is on. On macOS it allocates with the Mach VM, which the sanitizer does not intercept, so it never sees a page range change hands and reports the first write into recycled memory as a race - 30 of them in this test, and every one of them false.
